My smartwatch logged 'lying on the couch, thinking about running' as a workout and gave me a medal for effort.
My smart fridge judged my midnight snacking so hard it locked itself and left a note: "Talk to your feelings, not me."
I told my plants I was going on holiday. They died of abandonment issues before I even packed.
The librarian shushed me so hard my thoughts went quiet for a week.
My therapist says I catastrophise, which is exactly what someone would say right before everything falls apart.
My smoke alarm goes off every time I cook, which is how I know it believes in me.
I asked my GPS for the fastest route to success. It's been 'recalculating' for six years.
My bank flagged my salary as suspicious activity — even my own money doesn't believe I earned it.
I told my phone I needed space, so it deleted my photos and kept every screenshot of a parking spot.
I set my alarm for 6 a.m. to seize the day; the day filed a restraining order by 6:05.
